neighbours.label: verbs of spatial location ('situated', 'located', 'lay', 'placed') saying where something is
fire: The old monastery was situated high above the valley floor.
Our new office is located two blocks from the train station.
The farmhouse lay just south of the river crossing.
Three sensors were placed along the northern edge of the glacier.
The ruins are situated on a hill overlooking the harbour.
The embassy is located in the oldest quarter of the city.
Their summer cabin lay deep in the pine forest beyond the lake.
The lighthouse is situated at the tip of a rocky peninsula.
quiet: The old monastery was famous across the whole valley.
Our new office opened two weeks before the holidays.
The farmhouse burned down during the long drought.
Three sensors were damaged by the storm last winter.
The ruins are visited by tourists every single summer.
The embassy is closed for the national holiday tomorrow.
Their summer cabin needed a new roof after the snow.
The lighthouse is painted red and white every spring.

notes: Card: top 32 peak on ' located' x5, ' situated' x3, ' lay' x2, ' placed' x2, French 'situé', 'extended' (territory). Logit: + pole suppresses 'above/near/beneath', so the - pole pushes spatial prepositions next. Near misses keep the same subject and place phrase with a non-location verb.
